queries: WITH pr AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB * 1.0 / HCT) AS r FROM Laboratory WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL AND HCT IS NOT NULL AND HCT <> 0 GROUP BY ID), ov AS (SELECT AVG(r) AS a FROM pr), g1 AS (SELECT pr.ID, pr.r, pr.r - ov.a AS d1 FROM pr, ov WHERE pr.r > ov.a), ga AS (SELECT AVG(r) AS a FROM g1), g2 AS (SELECT g1.r, g1.d1, g1.r - ga.a AS d2 FROM g1, ga WHERE g1.r > ga.a) SELECT AVG(r) AS avg_ratio, AVG(d1) AS avg_above_overall, AVG(d2) AS avg_above_group FROM g2;

assumptions.assumption: A patient has multiple lab tests, so each patient's ratio is the mean of HGB/HCT over all of their lab rows with non-null HGB and non-zero, non-null HCT.
The 'overall average across all patients' is the unweighted mean of the per-patient ratios, and the 'group average' is the mean of the per-patient ratios in the first filtered group.
'How far above' means the simple difference (ratio minus the average), not a percentage.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat each lab test row (not each patient) as the unit: the overall average and group average are taken over individual HGB/HCT ratios.
alternatives.sql: WITH pr AS (SELECT ID, Date, HGB * 1.0 / HCT AS r FROM Laboratory WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL AND HCT IS NOT NULL AND HCT <> 0), ov AS (SELECT AVG(r) AS a FROM pr), g1 AS (SELECT pr.r, pr.r - ov.a AS d1 FROM pr, ov WHERE pr.r > ov.a), ga AS (SELECT AVG(r) AS a FROM g1), g2 AS (SELECT g1.r, g1.d1, g1.r - ga.a AS d2 FROM g1, ga WHERE g1.r > ga.a) SELECT AVG(r) AS avg_ratio, AVG(d1) AS avg_above_overall, AVG(d2) AS avg_above_group FROM g2;

assumptions.assumption: A patient's ratio is the mean of HGB/HCT over all their lab rows, so each patient counts once in every average.
Lab rows with NULL HGB or NULL/zero HCT are ignored.
The 'overall average' is the mean of the per-patient ratios, not the mean of all lab rows. The 'group average' is the mean ratio of the patients above the overall average.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat each lab test row as a unit, with no per-patient aggregation. The ratio is computed per row, and the two filters and averages run over rows.
alternatives.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT ID, HGB * 1.0 / HCT AS ratio FROM Laboratory WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL AND HCT IS NOT NULL AND HCT <> 0), g1 AS (SELECT ratio, ratio - (SELECT AVG(ratio) FROM r) AS above_overall FROM r WHERE ratio > (SELECT AVG(ratio) FROM r)), g2 AS (SELECT ratio, above_overall, ratio - (SELECT AVG(ratio) FROM g1) AS above_group FROM g1 WHERE ratio > (SELECT AVG(ratio) FROM g1)) SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio, AVG(above_overall) AS avg_above_overall, AVG(above_group) AS avg_above_group FROM g2

assumptions.assumption: A patient's ratio is the mean of HGB/HCT over all of their lab rows. Rows with a NULL or zero HGB or HCT are excluded. The request does not say how to combine a patient's multiple lab tests into one ratio.
The overall average is the unweighted mean of the per-patient ratios, over patients that have at least one valid lab row.
The group average is the mean ratio of the patients who passed the first filter. The second filter keeps patients strictly above it.

alternatives.interpretation: A patient's ratio is total HGB divided by total HCT across all of their lab rows (SUM(HGB)/SUM(HCT)), instead of the mean of the per-row ratios.
